user.title: Connect to the BioMatX bus
user.description: The RS485 inter-module bus is read through a serial adapter. Enter the serial device of the adapter, or a pyserial URL such as socket://host:port for an Ethernet gateway. BioMatX then listens to the bus for {seconds} seconds, without sending anything, to recognise the firmware and the modules.

data_description.device: Path such as /dev/serial/by-id/usb-FTDI_..., or a pyserial URL.

modules.title: Modules on the bus

data_description.module_count: Modules on the bus, 1 to 7, addressed 1 to 7 on their front panel.
data_description.all_off_scenario: Number (1 to 10) of the scenario programmed on every module to switch all relays off. Leave empty if none exists.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure the BioMatX bus
reconfigure.description: Change the serial device, or keep it to review the modules and the "all off" scenario on the next page. A device already read by the running integration is not opened a second time: the modules that integration has heard are shown instead. Entities keep their identifiers.

data_description.device: Path such as /dev/serial/by-id/usb-FTDI_..., or a pyserial URL.

error.cannot_connect: The serial device could not be opened. Check the path or URL and that the adapter is plugged in.

abort.already_configured: This serial device is already configured.

cannot_connect.message: Cannot open the BioMatX serial device {device}: {error}

link_down.message: The BioMatX bus is not connected; the command was not sent.

module_unavailable.message: BioMatX module {module} has not reported its state yet; the command was not sent.

not_confirmed.message: BioMatX module {module} did not confirm the command; check the light.
